behavioral_effects: Session files written through sandboxd now land in the fullstack_sandbox_workspaces named volume. Verified empirically: a file written through a live session is listed by the offline /workspaces/{id}/ls route (which returned [] for every workspace before the fix), appears in the volume, creates nothing under the daemon VM /workspaces, and survives a sandboxd restart through session reattach.

Offline workspace reads - the surface hibernation, workspace TTL sweeps, and the /workspaces/{id} routes depend on - now serve real content; before the fix they served the permanently empty volume view while sessions wrote to an unmanaged VM directory that a Docker Desktop reset would silently destroy.
compatibility_impact: Wire protocol and workspace ids unchanged; RemoteSandbox clients unaffected. The one real workspace (ws-a4c06bf0b73b) had its files migrated into the volume before the switch. The volume name is now pinned to fullstack_sandbox_workspaces regardless of COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME. A daemon with a non-default data-root must adjust the x-sandbox-workspace-root anchor per the compose comment.
follow_up: Add a sandbox smoke validator that writes through a live session and reads the same file back through the offline workspace API, so the DooD identity cannot silently regress.
Fix the services.json extractor to parse long-syntax volume mounts or fail loudly on them.
Consider an upstream pydantic-ai-backend issue proposing a separate daemon-side workspace-root variable for docker-outside-of-docker deployments.
limitations: The upstream library still conflates the path sandboxd reads with the path the daemon binds in one SANDBOXD_WORKSPACE_ROOT; the durable fix is a second daemon-side path variable upstream, not filed yet.
No registered validator asserts cross-view persistence (write through a live session, read through the offline API); this session verified it manually.
The services manifest extractor silently drops long-syntax service volume entries; worked around by keeping the mount in short syntax, extractor not fixed.
reason: Empirically verified docker-outside-of-docker path mismatch: sandboxd resolves SANDBOXD_WORKSPACE_ROOT in its own mount namespace but passes the string as a bind source to the host daemon, so session files land in an unmanaged docker-desktop VM directory while the sandbox_workspaces named volume stays empty and the offline workspace read API returns empty for workspaces that have files (ADR-006)
risks: The mountpoint path hardcodes the local volume driver layout (/var/lib/docker/volumes/<name>/_data); a daemon with a custom data-root silently re-creates the mismatch. The compose comment names docker volume inspect --format {{.Mountpoint}} as the source of truth for such hosts.
rollback: Revert the docker-compose.yml and docker/sandboxd/Dockerfile edits and recreate sandboxd with SANDBOX_SERVICE_TOKEN set. A revert does not restore: files written after this fix live in the named volume, which a reverted sandboxd neither reads nor binds (it would return to the mismatched /workspaces path), and the stale pre-fix data in the daemon VM /workspaces tree (smoke-session clones and probe files) was removed after migration and cannot be recovered.
security_impact: None added: sandboxd already held the Docker socket (root-equivalent by construction). Session data now lands inside the Docker-managed named volume instead of an unmanaged directory in the daemon VM root, which improves containment and auditability. Network posture, approval gating, and the wire protocol are unchanged.
summary: Fix the sandboxd workspace bind so session files actually land in the named volume

validators_run.evidence_ref: passes with MINIO_ROOT_USER/MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD supplied as CI does; fails without them for reasons unrelated to this change
